## Khiva and Bukhara: two People's Soviet Republics {uzbekistan turkmenistan}

In the former protectorate of the Khanate of Khiva, the Turkmen tribal leader Junaid Khan was made commander-in-chief of the khan's army in January 1918 and became the power in the land at the head of some 1,600 horsemen. In 1918 he killed Asfandiyar Khan (sources date this from the spring to October) and installed the late khan's uncle Said Abdulla as a figurehead while keeping real power for himself. The Young Khivans, opponents of Junaid's dictatorship, joined forces with Turkmen chiefs hostile to him and appealed to the Turkkomissiya, which sanctioned a military expedition. The Red Army crossed the Amu Darya on 25 December 1919 and on 22–23 January 1920 took Junaid's seat at Bedirkend. Persuaded by the commission's envoy Skalov, Said Abdulla signed a manifesto of abdication on 2 February. Skalov reported the former khan's remark that Khiva would live "under your wing" and noted that real power would rest with the Russian mission. On 26 April the First Khorezm Kurultai proclaimed the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic and adopted a constitution that preserved private ownership of land and the means of production. A treaty with Russia on 13 September recognised Khorezm's full independence, but before the year was out the Soviets deposed the Young Khivan government, and the nationalists went over to Junaid. [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [29](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_(1919%E2%80%941920)) [30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khorezm_People's_Soviet_Republic) [31](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%BC%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement)

In Bukhara, reform was pursued by the Young Bukharans, a Jadid group founded as a secret society in 1909. When they told the Bolsheviks in March 1918 that the people of Bukhara were waiting for revolution, Kolesov led troops to the city gates in person and demanded that Emir Said Alim Khan hand over power. According to Russian accounts the emir killed the Bolshevik delegation and proclaimed a holy war; thousands of Russians in and around Bukhara were killed and many Young Bukharans executed. Faizulla Khodzhayev, who escaped to Tashkent and was sentenced to death in absentia, later admitted that they had been "gullible" and had underestimated the clergy's influence and the strength of the old regime. For the next two years both sides prepared for a showdown behind a façade of truce. The emir ordered a mobilisation in February 1920, and former tsarist officers and White veterans found refuge at his court. As late as March 1920 Frunze told the emir that Soviet Russia was "interested in the highest degree" in Bukhara's territorial integrity, but on 3 August 1920 the Bolsheviks and the Young Bukharans agreed to act together, and on 16 August the Fourth Congress of the Bukharan Communist Party, meeting in Chardzhou, resolved to overthrow the emir. [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukharan_People's_Soviet_Republic) [33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Bukharans) [34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayzulla_Xo%CA%BBjayev) [6](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2,_%D0%A4%D1%91%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%80_%D0%98%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [35](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D1%83%D1%85%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_(1920))

At the end of August Young Bukharans and Bukharan communists rose in Chardzhou, and the Red Army, presenting its intervention as "revolutionary fraternal help", launched the Bukhara operation on 29 August. According to the Russian-language source the Turkestan Front committed 6,000–7,000 infantry, 2,300–2,690 cavalry, 8 armoured cars, 5 armoured trains and 11 aircraft, against roughly 16,000 regular troops of the emir and more than 27,000 irregulars raised by provincial governors. When the first two days of attacks stalled before the walls, command was unified on 31 August under Georgy Zinoviev, commander of the 1st Army, and heavy guns including 152-mm fortress pieces were brought up close. Some 12,000 shells were fired into the city, and the Russian-language source says that not a few of them were chemical. The Red Army broke through the Karshi Gate on 1 September and took the city, and on 2 September Frunze telegraphed Lenin that "the red banner... is flying over the Registan". The emir had already slipped away to eastern Bukhara on the night of 30–31 August with an escort of about 1,000 men. The Ark citadel was reduced to ruins by artillery and air attack, and hundreds of civilians were killed. On 8 October the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was proclaimed, with Khodzhayev as chairman of the Council of People's Nazirs (ministers). [35](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D1%83%D1%85%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_(1920)) [36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukhara_operation_(1920)) [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukharan_People's_Soviet_Republic) [34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayzulla_Xo%CA%BBjayev)

In Soviet terminology the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was a "revolutionary-democratic dictatorship", a transitional stage on the way to a socialist republic. Its constitution of September 1921, unlike the Russian one, recognised private ownership of land and the means of production and gave non-proletarians the vote, and Article 26 laid down that no law could contradict the fundamental principles of Islam. The aksakal system, under which villages chose their own representatives, was kept. Uzbek became the state language in place of Persian, the language of the elite, and the education nazir Abdurauf Fitrat sent many students to European, especially German, universities. The flag added a crescent to the hammer and sickle. Two weeks after the republic was proclaimed, Communist Party membership had swelled to 14,000, but a series of expulsions cut it to 1,000 by 1922. On 7 July 1922 Khodzhayev survived a Basmachi assassination attempt. From 1923 Moscow stepped up the pressure, accusing the Bukharan government of "bourgeois nationalism", and sweeping purges hit the government and the party. Khorezm, too, became a Socialist Soviet Republic in October 1923 and joined the USSR. ## The Soviet Republic of Gilan, Persia, 1920–1921 {iran soviet}

In Gilan, the Persian province on the southern shore of the Caspian, Mirza Kuchik Khan, a native of Rasht and a veteran of the Constitutional Revolution, had since 1914 led the Jungle (Jangali) movement from its base in the forests. Defeated at Manjil by the British and Bicherakhov's Cossacks in June 1918, it came to terms with the British in August, but when British troops entered Rasht in March 1919 with the support of landlords and mullahs it turned against them again. By then communists such as Ehsanollah Khan and non-Marxist Islamic socialists such as Kuchik Khan were organising separately within the movement. In the spring of 1920 the White Caspian Flotilla, beaten in South Russia, lay interned at the British-held port of Enzeli. On 17 May, just after the Sovietisation of Azerbaijan, the Volga–Caspian Flotilla under Fyodor Raskolnikov, with Grigory Ordzhonikidze aboard, sailed from Baku, and on 18 May off Enzeli it sent an ultimatum demanding that the British withdraw and hand over the military stores. When some 2,000 landing troops cut the road east of the town and cavalry closed it from the west, the British accepted and fell back to Rasht. The Soviets recovered 23 ships, 4 seaplanes and 50 guns. On 23 May People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs Georgy Chicherin assured the Iranian government that the operation had been carried out without the Soviet government's knowledge. [37](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AD%D0%BD%D0%B7%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_(1920)) [38](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fyodor_Raskolnikov) [39](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza_Kuchik_Khan) [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_Movement_of_Gilan) [41](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%93%D0%B8%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0)

Kuchik Khan agreed to cooperate on condition that he would lead the republic and that the Soviets would not interfere directly in its internal affairs. Having taken Rasht on 4 June, the Jangalis proclaimed the Socialist Soviet Republic of Gilan on 5 June, with Seyyed Jafar Pishevari as commissar for foreign affairs. The republic did not distribute land to poor peasants, however, and conflict soon broke out between Kuchik Khan and the Communist Party of Persia, which had grown out of the Baku-based Edalat party, and his deputy Ehsanollah Khan, who had become a communist. Kuchik Khan left Rasht, and according to the article on the Jungle movement a coup removed him on 31 July. Yakov Blumkin, sent by the Cheka, helped foment the coup and became chief of staff of the Persian Red Army. Under the nominal government of Ehsanollah Khan real power lay with the Soviet commissar Abukov, and radical measures such as anti-religious propaganda and levies on the rich alienated the middle classes and the clergy. An offensive aimed at Tehran in August was thrown back by Iranian troops. [42](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Socialist_Soviet_Republic) [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_Movement_of_Gilan) [41](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%93%D0%B8%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakov_Blumkin)

Moscow's calculations soon changed. In September 1920 the Russian government decided to wind up its military operation in Iran and negotiate with the Shah's government, and on 26 February 1921 Chicherin and Lev Karakhan signed the Russo-Persian Treaty of Friendship with Iran's envoy in Moscow. The treaty annulled the tsarist treaties, Turkmenchay among them, and gave both countries equal shipping rights on the Caspian, while allowing Russian troops to enter Iran if a third power used it as a base against Russia. That same month Reza Khan staged a coup in Tehran. The Soviet envoy in Tehran, Fyodor Rothstein, corresponded with Kuchik Khan urging withdrawal and told the Soviet officers in Ehsanollah Khan's force heading for Qazvin not to obey his orders. The Red Army began leaving in April 1921 and was gone by 8 September. Kuchik Khan, who had again taken charge of the government, struck on 29 September and killed the communist leader Heydar Khan Amu-oghli; amid the infighting government troops took Rasht. Fleeing into the mountains, Kuchik Khan froze to death on 2 December, and his severed head was displayed in Rasht. On the reasons for the withdrawal, Cosroe Chaqueri points to a Soviet shift from world revolution to the security of the Soviet state, while Kayhan Nejad argues that the infighting between communists and non-communists came first. ## Enver Pasha, the Basmachi decline and the delimitation of 1924 {tajikistan uzbekistan}

The fall of Bukhara set off a new Basmachi war in eastern Bukhara. Said Alim Khan fled via Dushanbe into exile in Kabul and directed the movement from there, while Ibrahim Bek of the Lakai tribe fought in the emir's name. In 1922 most of eastern Bukhara, from Hisor to the western Pamirs, was in Basmachi hands. Into this stepped Enver Pasha, the former Ottoman war minister. He had come to Moscow in August 1920, mixed with the Bolshevik leaders, and attended the Congress of the Peoples of the East in Baku in September. Trusted by the Soviets, he was sent to Bukhara in November 1921 but soon contacted rebel leaders and went over to the Basmachi. He drew the bands into a German-style command structure, for a time made himself supreme commander, and used a golden seal styling him "Commander-in-Chief of all the Armies of Islam". Ibrahim Bek distrusted him and at one point arrested him, and the emir broke with him in the first half of 1922. After Enver rejected a peace offer in May 1922 and demanded that the Red Army leave Turkestan within fifteen days, Red forces defeated the Basmachi at the Battle of Kafrun in June. He was killed on 4 August fighting Melkumov's cavalry near Baljuan or near Dushanbe; accounts of exactly how differ. [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukharan_People's_Soviet_Republic) [45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayyid_Mir_Muhammad_Alim_Khan) [46](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enver_Pasha) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [47](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B1%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%BC-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

The Soviet authorities paired overwhelming force with concessions. They restored sharia courts, Koran schools and waqf (religious endowment) lands, created a volunteer militia of Muslim peasants known as the "Red Sticks", and an estimated 15–25% of the Red Army troops in the region were Muslim. With civil-war veterans in the regular army now backed by air support, the movement crumbled. Enver's successor Selim Pasha fled to Afghanistan in 1923, and a large offensive in July–August 1923 drove the Basmachi out of Garm. In Fergana, Kurshirmat, who according to British intelligence had once commanded 5,000–6,000 men, was down to about 2,000 and left for Afghanistan in early 1923; by the first half of 1924 no bands remained in the valley. In the Tajik lands 200,000 people had fled and two-thirds of the arable land lay abandoned. An English-language source judges that the Basmachi were neither a genuine liberation movement nor a nationalist one but a temporary tribal alliance aimed at removing Russian rule, and that Enver's premature turn to semi-regular warfare inflicted losses from which it never recovered. In Khorezm, Junaid Khan, who with the backing of the Muslim clergy had built his forces up to 9,000 men, rose again at the end of 1923 and in January 1924 besieged Khiva and Novo-Urgench; the Red Army did not defeat him decisively until the end of 1924. Ibrahim Bek withdrew to Afghanistan in 1926 but kept raiding across the border until he was executed in 1931. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [48](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibrahim_Bek) [47](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B1%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%BC-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

The last stage was the drawing of borders. National delimitation had been discussed since 1920, and on 25 February 1924 the Bolshevik leadership announced that it would go ahead in Central Asia. Uzbek, Turkmen and Kazakh sub-committees worked fast, and in April it was decided to dissolve the Bukharan and Khorezm republics as well. Their communist parties objected openly; the Khorezm party in particular had to be strong-armed in July into voting for its own republic's dissolution. Bukhara, renamed a Socialist Soviet Republic on 19 September, disappeared little more than a month later. On 27 October 1924 the Turkestan Autonomous Republic, Bukhara and Khorezm were divided into the Uzbek SSR, the Turkmen SSR, a Tajik Autonomous Republic inside the Uzbek SSR, and the Kara-Kirghiz and Kara-Kalpak Autonomous Oblasts of the RSFSR, while much of Syr Darya province and half of Jetysu went to the Kirghiz (Kazakh) Autonomous Republic. An English-language source writes that Ryskulov and others who wanted to keep Turkestan whole were pitted against Khodzhayev and Akmal Ikramov, who favoured smaller units, and that the latter won; yet at his trial in 1938 Khodzhayev "confessed" to having opposed the breakup into four republics. In December 1924 he became chairman of the Uzbek Revolutionary Committee and led the new republic's government. [19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_delimitation_in_the_Soviet_Union) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%90%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic) [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukharan_People's_Soviet_Republic) [31](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%BC%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayzulla_Xo%CA%BBjayev)

## Assessments: anti-colonial revolution or continued Russian rule? {uzbekistan kazakhstan turkmenistan}

Soviet historiography described the period as "the struggle of the peoples of Central Asia for Soviet power". The Basmachi appeared as counter-revolutionary brigands driven by Islamic fundamentalism and backed by Britain and America, and the upheavals in Khiva and Bukhara in 1920 as fraternal aid to popular revolutions. After the Soviet collapse, the Central Asian states reversed the verdict: the Basmachi were recast as a national liberation movement in defence of the faith and their leaders as national heroes. The Uzbek historian Rajabov proposed treating the Kokand Autonomy, the Jadids and the Basmachi as one independence movement, a view shared by the émigré historian Baymirza Hayit. Against this, Alexander Morrison of Oxford argues that the Fergana Basmachi had no clear political aims and that Ibrahim Bek, acting nominally for the emir, was largely concerned with carving out a personal domain around Surkhandarya, and he rejects the idea that a single "Turkestani" identity drove mass resistance. Marie Bennigsen-Broxup concluded that the Basmachi had neither a political programme nor any vision of a liberated Turkestan, that theirs was the struggle of a threatened and ruined rural community to preserve its traditional values and way of life, and that the anti-Muslim policies of the Turksovnarkom fuelled the revolt. [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [47](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B1%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%BC-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

Views also divide over revolutionary power itself. Kolesov's all-Russian Sovnarkom, the destruction of Kokand and a Bolshevism dominated by Russian settlers made tsarist and Soviet rule look identical, as an English-language source puts it. Even the Russian-language article on the Bukhara operation describes it as a blow dealt to Bukharan independence "by the military aggression of Soviet Russia". On the other hand, Moscow's intervention after 1919 brought native cadres into government and attacked the settlers' "great-power chauvinism"; the Bukharan constitution respected Islamic principles and private property; and under the indigenisation policies of the 1920s many Central Asians rose to high office in the republics. The delimitation of 1924 is often condemned as divide and rule, but an English-language source notes that the attempt to weigh ethnicity together with economic viability in mixed regions such as Fergana produced convoluted borders and large minorities, and that no one intended these lines to become international frontiers. At a party congress in 1930 Ryskulov said that Central Asia still bore the marks of tsarist colonial policy. He and Khodzhayev were executed in 1938 and Bukeikhanov in 1937, while Mustafa Shokay carried on Turkestani nationalism in exile in France. ## 1917: The Tashkent Soviet and settler power {uzbekistan russia}

The Russian Empire conquered Turkestan in the second half of the 19th century and ran it as a colony in all but name. Its native inhabitants were classed as inorodtsy, a legal category separate from Russians, and although they made up nearly 10% of the empire's population they had no seats in the 435-member State Duma. During the Stolypin reforms of 1906–1912 up to 500,000 peasant households moved from central Russia to the Kazakh steppe and Central Asia and took up land there. When the tsarist government ordered in June 1916 that Muslim men aged 19 to 43 be drafted for labour behind the front, resistance that began in Khujand in July spread to Fergana, Semirechye and the Kazakh steppe. Settlers and natives massacred one another, and estimates of those who died directly or indirectly from the suppression range from about 100,000 to 500,000; hundreds of thousands of Kyrgyz and Kazakhs fled to China. Kyrgyz historiography holds that as many as 40% of the Kyrgyz died during the revolt or its aftermath. The Russian state had not restored order in parts of the region by the time of the October Revolution, and the experience shaped how natives would view Russian power in the revolutionary years. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asian_revolt_of_1916) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomy) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement)

After the February Revolution, Turkestan's Muslim intelligentsia founded the Shuro-i Islomiya (Muslim Council), dominated by Jadid reformers, in March 1917, while conservative ulama who put sharia first split off as the Ulamo Jamiyati. Real power in Tashkent, however, lay with the Tashkent Soviet of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies, made up of Russian railway workers and soldiers. Having clashed with the local organs of the Russian Provisional Government, the Soviet rose in arms in November and took Tashkent by 14 November (1 November O.S.). The Third Regional Congress of Soviets, meeting at the same time, set up a Sovnarkom but ignored native demands for autonomy. When a parallel Muslim congress proposed a coalition, the Turkestan Sovnarkom chairman Fyodor Kolesov refused, saying that "the inclusion of Muslims in the organ of supreme regional power is unacceptable at the present time"; not one of its fourteen commissars was a native. According to the Russian-language source, the Bolshevik Central Committee criticised the decision and demanded that native representatives be included. To the overwhelming Muslim majority, revolutionary power looked like a continuation of the tsarist colonial order. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomy) [4](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%B0%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%8F) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%90%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [6](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2,_%D0%A4%D1%91%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%80_%D0%98%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement)

## The Kokand Autonomy and the massacre of February 1918 {uzbekistan}

In answer to the Tashkent Sovnarkom's refusal, the Muslim movement held its Fourth Extraordinary All-Muslim Regional Congress in Kokand, the commercial centre of the Fergana Valley that lay beyond the Soviet's reach. On 10 December 1917 (27 November O.S.) some 200–250 delegates declared Turkestan "territorially autonomous in union with the federal democratic Russian republic". This was the Turkestan Autonomy, usually called the Kokand Autonomy. It had a 54-seat Provisional People's Council and a twelve-member provisional government; its first prime minister was the Kazakh Mukhamedzhan Tynyshpaev, and Mustafa Shokay ran external relations. The government announced that a parliament would be elected by universal, direct, equal and secret ballot on 20 March 1918, with two-thirds of the seats reserved for Muslims and one-third guaranteed to non-Muslims. Most of the native population backed it: rallies thousands strong were held in Namangan, Samarkand and elsewhere, and 60,000 gathered in Tashkent. At a Tashkent rally on the Prophet's birthday (13 December O.S.) part of the crowd entered the new city to free prisoners; soldiers opened fire and several were killed, and the freed prisoners were summarily executed. Asked to recognise the Autonomy, People's Commissar for Nationalities Joseph Stalin replied that the workers of Turkestan should disperse the Tashkent commissariat "by force" if they had the power. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomy) [4](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%B0%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%8F) [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafa_Shokay)

The Autonomy had almost no means of governing. Unable to tax, it lived on a 3-million-ruble loan and donations, and when Soviet forces seized 8 million rubles from the Kokand branch of the State Bank, including the Autonomy's own account, its internal quarrels deepened; in early January (December O.S.) Tynyshpaev resigned and Shokay became prime minister. Its national army of about 2,000 men had no officers or trained soldiers and relied on the militia of Ergash, the Kokand police chief. Shokay travelled to Orenburg to discuss joining the South-Eastern Union with Alexander Dutov but rejected its plan for a Cossack-dominated state; the Alash Autonomy put off any union until the Constituent Assembly met; and the Emir of Bukhara refused even to receive the Autonomy's envoys. In mid-January the Fourth Regional Congress of Soviets outlawed the Autonomy and ordered the arrest of its members. Once Dutov's blockade of the railway was lifted in January and arms could reach Tashkent, the military imbalance became decisive. Inside the Autonomy the conflict between the Jadid government and the conservatives sharpened, and on 18 February Ergash overthrew Shokay's government and took power himself. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomy) [4](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%B0%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%8F) [8](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%B9,_%D0%9C%D1%83%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%84%D0%B0)

In mid-February armed groups on the Autonomy's side seized the Palace of Khudayar Khan and the headquarters of the Kokand Soviet; the Tashkent Soviet declared martial law and sent troops under Konstantin Osipov. According to the Russian-language source, eleven trainloads of troops with artillery arrived, and armed Armenian Dashnak units fought alongside them. After talks broke down the Soviet forces shelled the palace, and when Ergash rejected an ultimatum to surrender on 19 February they shelled the city heavily. Fires spread, organised resistance collapsed, and on 22 February a delegation from the old city agreed to disarm and recognise Soviet authority. The captured city was sacked and its inhabitants massacred. Even the English-language sources disagree on the toll: the article on the Turkestan Autonomy says more than 10,000 residents were killed, the article on the Basmachi movement up to 25,000. The Soviet government requisitioned food from the region and caused a famine; supporters of the Autonomy were summarily executed or arrested, and in May 1918 the Tashkent branch of the Ulamo Jamiyati was dissolved. On 30 April the Fifth Regional Congress of Soviets proclaimed the Turkestan Soviet Republic, but it was not the national autonomy the Autonomy's supporters had fought for. ## The besieged Turkestan Soviet Republic, 1918–1919 {turkmenistan uzbekistan uk}

The Turkestan Soviet Republic proclaimed on 30 April 1918 called itself an autonomous republic of the Russian Federation, but, as an English-language source puts it, at first it controlled only a few railway junctions. By the summer the Orenburg Cossacks and the fronts of the civil war had cut it off from Russia. Moscow's dispatch in June of 70 million rubles and 115 wagons of grain from Tsaritsyn was for a long time the last major help. Because natives were not subject to conscription until the summer of 1920, the republic's Red Army numbered only about 8,000 in the summer of 1918 and about 20,000 by the spring of 1919; at the end of 1918 some 2,500 internationalists, former Austro-Hungarian prisoners of war, were fighting at the front. The area sown to cotton fell from 523,000 desyatinas in 1915 to 80,000 in 1918, and total sown area in the Syr Darya, Samarkand and Fergana provinces shrank by 46% in a single year. On 27 December 1918 the Turkestan Central Executive Committee declared the republic a "military camp". When Eastern Front troops took Orenburg on 22 January 1919 and briefly broke the blockade, Moscow sent military stores and 2 million poods of grain and Turkestan sent 350 wagons of cotton in return, but in April Dutov's forces cut the railway again, opening the Aktyubinsk front. [9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%90%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Dutov)

Rebellion broke out to the west as well, in Transcaspia. In June 1918 an attempt by the Ashgabat Soviet to register all men bearing arms set off two days of rioting; Frolov, sent from Tashkent, personally shot five railwaymen who came to present a petition and was then killed by armed workers at Kizyl-Arvat. On 11–12 July the railway workers of Ashgabat rose and set up a Socialist Revolutionary–Menshevik government, the Transcaspian Government, headed by the SR Fyodor Funtikov. Defeated near Chardzhou, it appealed to the British mission in Mashhad and on 19 August concluded an agreement with General Wilfrid Malleson. British Indian troops fought at Bairam Ali and Kaakha, defeated the Bolsheviks at the Battle of Dushak on 14 October and pushed them back to Merv. The execution of the 26 Baku Commissars under this government on 20 September is covered in "Revolution and war in Transcaucasia". With no economy of its own the government depended on British money, and in January 1919, amid workers' unrest, it gave way to a committee picked by a British officer. Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia then took over this front; after the British withdrew in the spring of 1919, the Red Army took Ashgabat on 9 July and all of Transcaspia by February 1920. [11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcaspian_Government) [12](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%97%D0%B0%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BF%D0%B8%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B5_%D0%B2%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B5_%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D1%8C%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleson_mission)

The gravest crisis came inside Tashkent itself. After the anti-Bolshevik underground Turkestan Military Organisation was uncovered in the autumn of 1918, the surviving conspirators formed a "Council of Five" and drew in Konstantin Osipov, the republic's military commissar. When the rising began on the evening of 18 January 1919, the chairman of the Central Executive Committee Votintsev, the chairman of the Tashkent Soviet Shumilov, the head of the Turkestan Cheka Fomenko and others who went to Osipov to find out what was happening were shot at once on his orders; ten more died over the next two days, and the republic's leadership was all but wiped out. But the railway workshop workers held their arsenal, and Ivan Belov, the Left SR commandant of the fortress whose garrison was largely made up of Hungarian internationalists, shelled the rebel headquarters with howitzers. By 20 January the revolt had failed, and Osipov fled with Turkestan's gold reserve through Chimkent into the mountains. He joined the Basmachi leader Madamin Bek in Fergana, moved on to Bukhara, and then disappears from the record. A provisional revolutionary military council formed on 21 January appealed to the Russian Sovnarkom for help. ## The Kazakh steppe: the choices of the Alash Orda {kazakhstan}

Kazakh intellectuals had worked with the Constitutional Democrats (Kadets) since 1905, and in the summer of 1917 they broke away to form the Alash party. Alikhan Bukeikhanov had been appointed the Russian Provisional Government's commissioner for Turgay Oblast in March 1917. In April an All-Kazakh Congress that he, Akhmet Baitursynov and others convened in Orenburg demanded that lands confiscated by the old regime be returned to the native population and the new settlers expelled, that local schools be handed to natives, and that the 1916 conscription be ended. After the October Revolution the Second All-Kazakh Congress, held in Orenburg on 18–26 December 1917 (5–13 December O.S.), resolved to create a Kazakh autonomy, Alash, with a 25-member People's Council, the Alash Orda, in which ten seats were reserved for Russians and other non-Kazakhs. Bukeikhanov was its chairman and Semipalatinsk its capital. A proposal by the Dosmukhamedov brothers to proclaim autonomy immediately lost by 33 votes to 40. Wary as they were of the Bolsheviks, the Alash leaders at first kept up contacts, and the Dosmukhamedovs met Lenin and Stalin. But in the spring of 1918 rival authorities on the steppe left disorder and violence in their wake, and the leaders had to hide from the Red Army. [15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alash_Autonomy) [16](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%88-%D0%9E%D1%80%D0%B4%D0%B0) [17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alikhan_Bukeikhanov)

After the revolt of the Czechoslovak Legion, most of present-day Kazakhstan was in anti-Bolshevik hands by the summer of 1918, and the Alash Orda leaned towards the Whites. On 11 June it declared all Soviet decrees on its territory void; its western branch dealt with the Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly (Komuch) in Samara, its eastern branch with the Siberian government in Omsk, and its Turgay branch with Dutov. Komuch formally recognised the Alash autonomy in early September and granted it 3 million rubles, but the Siberian government refused to recognise national autonomies. The Alash Orda trained Kazakh horsemen under Russian officer-instructors, and in June 1918 a Kazakh cavalry detachment of 300–500 men entered Semipalatinsk after the Bolsheviks left. Its military council asked for cavalry corps totalling 26,000 men, but the Siberian government allowed only one cavalry regiment, the Orenburg Cossack government helped form two, and Komuch paid for a people's army of 2,000 for the western branch. On 4 November the Ufa Directory abolished all autonomies on its territory, and Alexander Kolchak, who seized power soon afterwards, was firmly opposed to national autonomy. At a conference in Omsk in February 1919 Bukeikhanov denied any separatism—"We are Westerners... we can obtain culture through Russia"—but won no decision. [16](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%88-%D0%9E%D1%80%D0%B4%D0%B0) [15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alash_Autonomy)

Cold-shouldered by the Whites, the Alash leaders began negotiating with the Soviet government in the spring of 1919. In March 1919 a Kazakh unit in Turgay made supporters of Bukeikhanov and Baitursynov recognise Soviet power, and Akhmet Baitursynov himself went to negotiate and urged other Alash figures to break with the Whites. After secret talks the western branch also turned neutral, weakening the White offensive. The Russian Sovnarkom set up a Revolutionary Committee for the Kirghiz (Kazakh) Territory on 10 July 1919, and the Red Army's Eastern Front counter-offensive that summer brought all of present-day Kazakhstan under Bolshevik control. On 10 December the western branch recognised Soviet power, and Bukeikhanov of the eastern branch followed. Despite the promised amnesty, the Alash Orda was abolished in early March 1920. On 26 August 1920 the Kirghiz Autonomous Socialist Soviet Republic was founded with its capital at Orenburg—"Kirghiz" then meant the Kazakhs. Alash leaders took various posts but most were executed in the 1930s; Bukeikhanov was shot in 1937. ## The rise of the Basmachi: Fergana, 1918–1920 {uzbekistan kyrgyzstan tajikistan}

"Basmachi" is Uzbek for "bandits", a name the Soviet side used to paint the resistance as criminals; the fighters called themselves mujahideen. The roots ran deep. Under Russian rule the Fergana Valley had been turned into a cotton monoculture, indebted farmers and a landless rural proletariat multiplied, and the revolt of 1916 was the first mass anti-Russian rising. The Kokand massacre and the execution of Fergana peasants suspected of hoarding cotton and food enraged the Muslim population. Ergash fought on as self-styled "Supreme Leader of the Islamic Army", and as nationalisations from Tashkent wrecked the economy and the loss of grain imports brought famine, people joined in large numbers. An English-language source puts the scattered bands at roughly 20,000 men by the end of 1918; the Russian-language source says Ergash's forces alone reached 25,000 by November, with nearly 40 other bands besides. Madamin Bek, a former militia chief of Old Margilan, refused to accept Ergash's leadership and built up his own following; by 1919 he controlled most of the valley outside the large towns and the railways. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [21](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9C%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D0%BD-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

To defend themselves against Basmachi raids, Russian settlers formed the Peasant Army of Fergana in the spring of 1919, about 20,000 men commanded by the retired colonel Konstantin Monstrov. At first it fought the Basmachi alongside the Bolsheviks, but as resentment of the Cheka and grain requisitioning grew it allied with Madamin Bek at the end of August 1919. Together they took Osh and attacked Andijan in September, only to be beaten by reinforcements including a Kazan regiment. On 22 October a "Fergana Provisional Government" was formed with Madamin Bek at its head and Monstrov as his deputy, envisaging a joint Russian–Muslim state, but quarrels over its Islamic character soon broke up the alliance. Monstrov surrendered to the Bolsheviks on 17 January 1920, and after a string of defeats in February Madamin Bek, surrounded, signed an agreement recognising Soviet power on 6 March. Mikhail Frunze, commander of the Turkestan Front, attended a celebratory parade in Fergana on 20 March. Sent to win over other kurbashi, Madamin Bek was captured and killed in May 1920 by the bands of Kurshirmat and Khal-Khodzha. When the Soviet authorities resumed food requisitioning and the conscription of Muslims in the summer of 1920, Kurshirmat gathered an "Army of Islam" and the revolt flared up again. [22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasant_Army_of_Fergana) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [21](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9C%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D0%BD-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

Calm in Fergana did not last. Kurshirmat (Sher Muhammad Bek), who took Madamin Bek's place as leader, gathered a number of bands into an "Army of Islam" in the summer of 1920 and went on the offensive around Andijan, Jalal-Abad, Osh, Kokand and Namangan. When Frunze diverted troops to the Bukhara expedition the Basmachi regrouped, and by the end of the year the movement had spread widely again. In the autumn of 1920 the Turkestan Front under Grigory Sokolnikov carried out three sweeps of the Fergana Valley that drove the bands to the gorges on its edges; a report by the front staff noted that some bands had returned to peasant life "for the time being". By April 1921 most of the large bands had been defeated. The Soviet side also sent Muslim units against the Basmachi, such as the Dungan Cavalry Regiment formed by the Dungan Magaza Masanchi. Meanwhile in Samarkand province Muslim rebels and clergy declared independence in November 1918, and 9,000 cavalry and 4,000 foot from the Matcha district on the upper Zeravshan seized Panjakent and the Ura-Tyube and Khujand districts in the autumn of 1919. The Red Army did not retake the area until March 1923. ## Frunze and the Turkkomissiya: Moscow returns, and the Muslim communists {uzbekistan soviet}

Kolchak's defeat changed the situation in Turkestan. In August 1919 the Southern Group of the Eastern Front was reorganised as the Turkestan Front, and on 15 August Mikhail Frunze took command. After smashing Kolchak's Southern Army, the Turkestan Front linked up with the Turkestan republic's forces on 13 September, restoring the connection with Moscow. Political control lay with the Turkestan Commission (Turkkomissiya). It had been created in February 1919 under Shalva Eliava but, held up by Kolchak's advance, got no further than Samara and Orenburg; from October it acted with powers delegated by the All-Russian Central Executive Committee, the Sovnarkom and the Bolshevik Central Committee, in effect as the supreme authority in the region. Valerian Kuibyshev joined it as deputy chairman and as a member of the Turkestan Front's Revolutionary Military Council. The commission took a direct part in founding the Communist Party of Turkestan in January 1920, and in March 1920 it revived the Turkestan Sovnarkom under Jānis Rudzutaks. Between February and December 1920 the Turkkomissiya alone received 614 wagons of goods, while Turkestan shipped cotton and wool to the centre. The commission was dissolved in August 1920, and its role in guiding the party passed to the Turkestan Bureau of the Bolshevik Central Committee. [23](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9_%D1%84%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%82) [24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Frunze) [25](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AD%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%B0,_%D0%A8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B2%D0%B0_%D0%97%D1%83%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [26](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D1%83%D0%B9%D0%B1%D1%8B%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%B2,_%D0%92%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BD_%D0%92%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%90%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0)

As Moscow set out to bring natives into government, Muslim communists came to the fore. Turar Ryskulov, a Kazakh who had taken part in the 1916 revolt, became chairman of the Muslim Bureau of the Turkestan Communist Party in 1919 and chairman of the Turkestan Central Executive Committee in January 1920. Holding that the Turkic peoples of Turkestan were a single nation divided only by history, he argued that the republic should be renamed a "Turkic Republic", the party turned into a "Turkic Communist Party" separate from the Russian party, and non-Muslim units withdrawn. In a resolution of 8 March 1920 the Bolshevik Central Committee reaffirmed the party's name and Turkestan's status as an "autonomous republic of the RSFSR", reserving defence, foreign relations, railways and finance to the federal government. In May a delegation including Ryskulov set out its views in Moscow and was rebuffed as contrary to the party's nationalities policy; according to an English-language source, Vladimir Lenin summoned him personally and persuaded him to drop the idea. Ryskulov left the chairmanship in July, and in September the Ninth Congress of Soviets of Turkestan condemned the "national deviationists". In June 1923 Stalin accused him of "pan-Turkism" and of backing Mirsaid Sultan-Galiev. [27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turar_Ryskulov) [28](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A0%D1%8B%D1%81%D0%BA%D1%83%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%B2,_%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%80_%D0%A0%D1%8B%D1%81%D0%BA%D1%83%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A2%D1%83%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%90%D0%B2%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0)

Moscow's return also meant the arrival of War Communism. The Turkestan Central Executive Committee adopted a grain monopoly decree only on 4 June 1919 and, for want of preparation and in the face of kulak resistance, could not enforce it; in February 1920 it set up food-requisition squads and committees of the poor in villages with European populations and assigned requisition quotas to all settler peasants. From the autumn of 1920 requisitioning was extended to the native population, and some 8,500 people, mostly of local nationalities, were mobilised into requisition squads and units such as the "Muslim inspection". The Russian-language source notes that, unlike in the centre, part of the grain surplus could be sold on the market. In 1920 the distribution of feudal lords' land to working peasants began, and from late 1919 until March 1921 revolutionary committees exercised power in place of the executive committees of the soviets. Natives were not conscripted until the summer of 1920, but when Muslim conscription and food requisitioning resumed, revolt flared up again in Fergana. An English-language source quotes the historian Kotelnikov's view that the grain monopoly of 25 June 1919 was in effect a robbery of the peasants that caused famine in some places. ## Khiva and Bukhara: two People's Soviet Republics {uzbekistan turkmenistan}

In the former protectorate of the Khanate of Khiva, the Turkmen tribal leader Junaid Khan was made commander-in-chief of the khan's army in January 1918 and became the power in the land at the head of some 1,600 horsemen. In 1918 he killed Asfandiyar Khan (sources date this from the spring to October) and installed the late khan's uncle Said Abdulla as a figurehead while keeping real power for himself. The Young Khivans, opponents of Junaid's dictatorship, joined forces with Turkmen chiefs hostile to him and appealed to the Turkkomissiya, which sanctioned a military expedition. The Red Army crossed the Amu Darya on 25 December 1919 and on 22–23 January 1920 took Junaid's seat at Bedirkend. Persuaded by the commission's envoy Skalov, Said Abdulla signed a manifesto of abdication on 2 February. Skalov reported the former khan's remark that Khiva would live "under your wing" and noted that real power would rest with the Russian mission. On 26 April the First Khorezm Kurultai proclaimed the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic and adopted a constitution that preserved private ownership of land and the means of production. A treaty with Russia on 13 September recognised Khorezm's full independence, but before the year was out the Soviets deposed the Young Khivan government, and the nationalists went over to Junaid. [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [29](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_%281919%E2%80%941920%29) [30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khorezm_People's_Soviet_Republic) [31](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A5%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%BC%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement)

In Bukhara, reform was pursued by the Young Bukharans, a Jadid group founded as a secret society in 1909. When they told the Bolsheviks in March 1918 that the people of Bukhara were waiting for revolution, Kolesov led troops to the city gates in person and demanded that Emir Said Alim Khan hand over power. According to Russian accounts the emir killed the Bolshevik delegation and proclaimed a holy war; thousands of Russians in and around Bukhara were killed and many Young Bukharans executed. Faizulla Khodzhayev, who escaped to Tashkent and was sentenced to death in absentia, later admitted that they had been "gullible" and had underestimated the clergy's influence and the strength of the old regime. For the next two years both sides prepared for a showdown behind a façade of truce. The emir ordered a mobilisation in February 1920, and former tsarist officers and White veterans found refuge at his court. As late as March 1920 Frunze told the emir that Soviet Russia was "interested in the highest degree" in Bukhara's territorial integrity, but on 3 August 1920 the Bolsheviks and the Young Bukharans agreed to act together, and on 16 August the Fourth Congress of the Bukharan Communist Party, meeting in Chardzhou, resolved to overthrow the emir. At the end of August Young Bukharans and Bukharan communists rose in Chardzhou, and the Red Army, presenting its intervention as "revolutionary fraternal help", launched the Bukhara operation on 29 August. According to the Russian-language source the Turkestan Front committed 6,000–7,000 infantry, 2,300–2,690 cavalry, 8 armoured cars, 5 armoured trains and 11 aircraft, against roughly 16,000 regular troops of the emir and more than 27,000 irregulars raised by provincial governors. When the first two days of attacks stalled before the walls, command was unified on 31 August under Georgy Zinoviev, commander of the 1st Army, and heavy guns including 152-mm fortress pieces were brought up close. Some 12,000 shells were fired into the city, and the Russian-language source says that not a few of them were chemical. The Red Army broke through the Karshi Gate on 1 September and took the city, and on 2 September Frunze telegraphed Lenin that "the red banner... is flying over the Registan". The emir had already slipped away to eastern Bukhara on the night of 30–31 August with an escort of about 1,000 men. The Ark citadel was reduced to ruins by artillery and air attack, and hundreds of civilians were killed. On 8 October the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was proclaimed, with Khodzhayev as chairman of the Council of People's Nazirs (ministers). [35](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D1%83%D1%85%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_%281920%29) [36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukhara_operation_%281920%29) [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukharan_People's_Soviet_Republic) [34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayzulla_Xo%CA%BBjayev)

In Soviet terminology the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was a "revolutionary-democratic dictatorship", a transitional stage on the way to a socialist republic. Its constitution of September 1921, unlike the Russian one, recognised private ownership of land and the means of production and gave non-proletarians the vote, and Article 26 laid down that no law could contradict the fundamental principles of Islam. The aksakal system, under which villages chose their own representatives, was kept. Uzbek became the state language in place of Persian, the language of the elite, and the education nazir Abdurauf Fitrat sent many students to European, especially German, universities. The flag added a crescent to the hammer and sickle. Two weeks after the republic was proclaimed, Communist Party membership had swelled to 14,000, but a series of expulsions cut it to 1,000 by 1922. On 7 July 1922 Khodzhayev survived a Basmachi assassination attempt. From 1923 Moscow stepped up the pressure, accusing the Bukharan government of "bourgeois nationalism", and sweeping purges hit the government and the party. Khorezm, too, became a Socialist Soviet Republic in October 1923 and joined the USSR. ## The Soviet Republic of Gilan, Persia, 1920–1921 {iran soviet}

In Gilan, the Persian province on the southern shore of the Caspian, Mirza Kuchik Khan, a native of Rasht and a veteran of the Constitutional Revolution, had since 1914 led the Jungle (Jangali) movement from its base in the forests. Defeated at Manjil by the British and Bicherakhov's Cossacks in June 1918, it came to terms with the British in August, but when British troops entered Rasht in March 1919 with the support of landlords and mullahs it turned against them again. By then communists such as Ehsanollah Khan and non-Marxist Islamic socialists such as Kuchik Khan were organising separately within the movement. In the spring of 1920 the White Caspian Flotilla, beaten in South Russia, lay interned at the British-held port of Enzeli. On 17 May, just after the Sovietisation of Azerbaijan, the Volga–Caspian Flotilla under Fyodor Raskolnikov, with Grigory Ordzhonikidze aboard, sailed from Baku, and on 18 May off Enzeli it sent an ultimatum demanding that the British withdraw and hand over the military stores. When some 2,000 landing troops cut the road east of the town and cavalry closed it from the west, the British accepted and fell back to Rasht. The Soviets recovered 23 ships, 4 seaplanes and 50 guns. On 23 May People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs Georgy Chicherin assured the Iranian government that the operation had been carried out without the Soviet government's knowledge. [37](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AD%D0%BD%D0%B7%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D1%8F_%281920%29) [38](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fyodor_Raskolnikov) [39](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirza_Kuchik_Khan) [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_Movement_of_Gilan) [41](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%93%D0%B8%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%81%D0%BE%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0)

Kuchik Khan agreed to cooperate on condition that he would lead the republic and that the Soviets would not interfere directly in its internal affairs. Having taken Rasht on 4 June, the Jangalis proclaimed the Socialist Soviet Republic of Gilan on 5 June, with Seyyed Jafar Pishevari as commissar for foreign affairs. The republic did not distribute land to poor peasants, however, and conflict soon broke out between Kuchik Khan and the Communist Party of Persia, which had grown out of the Baku-based Edalat party, and his deputy Ehsanollah Khan, who had become a communist. Kuchik Khan left Rasht, and according to the article on the Jungle movement a coup removed him on 31 July. Yakov Blumkin, sent by the Cheka, helped foment the coup and became chief of staff of the Persian Red Army. Under the nominal government of Ehsanollah Khan real power lay with the Soviet commissar Abukov, and radical measures such as anti-religious propaganda and levies on the rich alienated the middle classes and the clergy. An offensive aimed at Tehran in August was thrown back by Iranian troops. Moscow's calculations soon changed. In September 1920 the Russian government decided to wind up its military operation in Iran and negotiate with the Shah's government, and on 26 February 1921 Chicherin and Lev Karakhan signed the Russo-Persian Treaty of Friendship with Iran's envoy in Moscow. The treaty annulled the tsarist treaties, Turkmenchay among them, and gave both countries equal shipping rights on the Caspian, while allowing Russian troops to enter Iran if a third power used it as a base against Russia. That same month Reza Khan staged a coup in Tehran. The Soviet envoy in Tehran, Fyodor Rothstein, corresponded with Kuchik Khan urging withdrawal and told the Soviet officers in Ehsanollah Khan's force heading for Qazvin not to obey his orders. The Red Army began leaving in April 1921 and was gone by 8 September. Kuchik Khan, who had again taken charge of the government, struck on 29 September and killed the communist leader Heydar Khan Amu-oghli; amid the infighting government troops took Rasht. Fleeing into the mountains, Kuchik Khan froze to death on 2 December, and his severed head was displayed in Rasht. On the reasons for the withdrawal, Cosroe Chaqueri points to a Soviet shift from world revolution to the security of the Soviet state, while Kayhan Nejad argues that the infighting between communists and non-communists came first. ## Enver Pasha, the Basmachi decline and the delimitation of 1924 {tajikistan uzbekistan}

The fall of Bukhara set off a new Basmachi war in eastern Bukhara. Said Alim Khan fled via Dushanbe into exile in Kabul and directed the movement from there, while Ibrahim Bek of the Lakai tribe fought in the emir's name. In 1922 most of eastern Bukhara, from Hisor to the western Pamirs, was in Basmachi hands. Into this stepped Enver Pasha, the former Ottoman war minister. He had come to Moscow in August 1920, mixed with the Bolshevik leaders, and attended the Congress of the Peoples of the East in Baku in September. Trusted by the Soviets, he was sent to Bukhara in November 1921 but soon contacted rebel leaders and went over to the Basmachi. He drew the bands into a German-style command structure, for a time made himself supreme commander, and used a golden seal styling him "Commander-in-Chief of all the Armies of Islam". Ibrahim Bek distrusted him and at one point arrested him, and the emir broke with him in the first half of 1922. After Enver rejected a peace offer in May 1922 and demanded that the Red Army leave Turkestan within fifteen days, Red forces defeated the Basmachi at the Battle of Kafrun in June. He was killed on 4 August fighting Melkumov's cavalry near Baljuan or near Dushanbe; accounts of exactly how differ. The Soviet authorities paired overwhelming force with concessions. They restored sharia courts, Koran schools and waqf (religious endowment) lands, created a volunteer militia of Muslim peasants known as the "Red Sticks", and an estimated 15–25% of the Red Army troops in the region were Muslim. With civil-war veterans in the regular army now backed by air support, the movement crumbled. Enver's successor Selim Pasha fled to Afghanistan in 1923, and a large offensive in July–August 1923 drove the Basmachi out of Garm. In Fergana, Kurshirmat, who according to British intelligence had once commanded 5,000–6,000 men, was down to about 2,000 and left for Afghanistan in early 1923; by the first half of 1924 no bands remained in the valley. In the Tajik lands 200,000 people had fled and two-thirds of the arable land lay abandoned. An English-language source judges that the Basmachi were neither a genuine liberation movement nor a nationalist one but a temporary tribal alliance aimed at removing Russian rule, and that Enver's premature turn to semi-regular warfare inflicted losses from which it never recovered. In Khorezm, Junaid Khan, who with the backing of the Muslim clergy had built his forces up to 9,000 men, rose again at the end of 1923 and in January 1924 besieged Khiva and Novo-Urgench; the Red Army did not defeat him decisively until the end of 1924. Ibrahim Bek withdrew to Afghanistan in 1926 but kept raiding across the border until he was executed in 1931. The last stage was the drawing of borders. National delimitation had been discussed since 1920, and on 25 February 1924 the Bolshevik leadership announced that it would go ahead in Central Asia. Uzbek, Turkmen and Kazakh sub-committees worked fast, and in April it was decided to dissolve the Bukharan and Khorezm republics as well. Their communist parties objected openly; the Khorezm party in particular had to be strong-armed in July into voting for its own republic's dissolution. Bukhara, renamed a Socialist Soviet Republic on 19 September, disappeared little more than a month later. On 27 October 1924 the Turkestan Autonomous Republic, Bukhara and Khorezm were divided into the Uzbek SSR, the Turkmen SSR, a Tajik Autonomous Republic inside the Uzbek SSR, and the Kara-Kirghiz and Kara-Kalpak Autonomous Oblasts of the RSFSR, while much of Syr Darya province and half of Jetysu went to the Kirghiz (Kazakh) Autonomous Republic. An English-language source writes that Ryskulov and others who wanted to keep Turkestan whole were pitted against Khodzhayev and Akmal Ikramov, who favoured smaller units, and that the latter won; yet at his trial in 1938 Khodzhayev "confessed" to having opposed the breakup into four republics. In December 1924 he became chairman of the Uzbek Revolutionary Committee and led the new republic's government. ## Assessments: anti-colonial revolution or continued Russian rule? {uzbekistan kazakhstan turkmenistan}

Soviet historiography described the period as "the struggle of the peoples of Central Asia for Soviet power". The Basmachi appeared as counter-revolutionary brigands driven by Islamic fundamentalism and backed by Britain and America, and the upheavals in Khiva and Bukhara in 1920 as fraternal aid to popular revolutions. After the Soviet collapse, the Central Asian states reversed the verdict: the Basmachi were recast as a national liberation movement in defence of the faith and their leaders as national heroes. The Uzbek historian Rajabov proposed treating the Kokand Autonomy, the Jadids and the Basmachi as one independence movement, a view shared by the émigré historian Baymirza Hayit. Against this, Alexander Morrison of Oxford argues that the Fergana Basmachi had no clear political aims and that Ibrahim Bek, acting nominally for the emir, was largely concerned with carving out a personal domain around Surkhandarya, and he rejects the idea that a single "Turkestani" identity drove mass resistance. Marie Bennigsen-Broxup concluded that the Basmachi had neither a political programme nor any vision of a liberated Turkestan, that theirs was the struggle of a threatened and ruined rural community to preserve its traditional values and way of life, and that the anti-Muslim policies of the Turksovnarkom fuelled the revolt. [20](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%91%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%BE) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basmachi_movement) [47](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B1%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%BC-%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA)

Views also divide over revolutionary power itself. Kolesov's all-Russian Sovnarkom, the destruction of Kokand and a Bolshevism dominated by Russian settlers made tsarist and Soviet rule look identical, as an English-language source puts it. Even the Russian-language article on the Bukhara operation describes it as a blow dealt to Bukharan independence "by the military aggression of Soviet Russia". On the other hand, Moscow's intervention after 1919 brought native cadres into government and attacked the settlers' "great-power chauvinism"; the Bukharan constitution respected Islamic principles and private property; and under the indigenisation policies of the 1920s many Central Asians rose to high office in the republics. The delimitation of 1924 is often condemned as divide and rule, but an English-language source notes that the attempt to weigh ethnicity together with economic viability in mixed regions such as Fergana produced convoluted borders and large minorities, and that no one intended these lines to become international frontiers. At a party congress in 1930 Ryskulov said that Central Asia still bore the marks of tsarist colonial policy. He and Khodzhayev were executed in 1938 and Bukeikhanov in 1937, while Mustafa Shokay carried on Turkestani nationalism in exile in France. ## 1918년 초: 첸트로시비리와 극동 인민위원회의 {russia}

10월 혁명 무렵 시베리아의 소비에트들은 이르쿠츠크에서 제1차 전시베리아 소비에트 대회를 열고, 이 대회에서 시베리아와 극동 전역의 소비에트를 이끌 중앙집행위원회, 곧 첸트로시비리를 세웠다. 대회에는 튜멘에서 블라디보스토크까지 70개 소비에트를 대표하는 대의원 약 185명이 모였고, 첸트로시비리 의장은 볼셰비키 보리스 슈먀츠키가 맡았다. 1917년 12월 이르쿠츠크에서는 사관생도와 카자크, 장교, 학생들이 소비에트에 맞서 봉기했다. 크라스노야르스크에서 온 적위대를 이끈 세르게이 라조는 시가전 끝에 한때 포로가 되었지만, 12월 29일 휴전 뒤 며칠 만에 이르쿠츠크의 소비에트 권력이 회복되었다. 1918년 2월 16일 이르쿠츠크에서 열린 제2차 전시베리아 소비에트 대회에서는 대의원 202명 가운데 볼셰비키가 123명, 좌파 사회혁명당이 53명이었고, 우파 사회혁명당은 7명으로 줄었다. 대회는 시베리아 소비에트 공화국의 이름으로, 소브나르콤이 독일과 맺을 강화에 구속되지 않겠다고 선언했다. 그러나 첸트로시비리 스스로 인정했듯 각지 소비에트는 제각기 움직이며 상급 기관의 지시를 자주 어겼다. [1](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B1%D0%B8%D1%80%D1%8C) [2](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9B%D0%B0%D0%B7%D0%BE,_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B3%D0%B5%D0%B9_%D0%93%D0%B5%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87)

극동에서는 1917년 7월 말 미국에서 돌아와 볼셰비키에 합류한 알렉산드르 크라스노쇼코프가 소비에트 권력 수립을 이끌었다. 그는 하바롭스크에 세워진 극동 인민위원회의 의장이 되었고, 1918년 여름 약 넉 달 동안 극동 전역을 장악했다. 하바롭스크 소비에트의 외무 인민위원은 조선인 볼셰비키 알렉산드라 킴이었다. 그녀는 1918년 봄 이동휘 등과 함께 한인사회당을 세우고 조선인 적위대를 조직했다. 그러나 이 권력은 얇았다. 1918년 1월 일본 전함들이 블라디보스토크항에 들어왔고, 자바이칼에서는 아타만 그리고리 세묘노프가 만주 쪽에서 국경을 넘나들며 공격해 왔다. 첸트로시비리는 봄에 라조를 사령관으로 하는 다우리야(자바이칼) 전선을 만들어 세묘노프와 싸우게 하고, 5월 8일 그를 인민의 적으로 선포했다. 아무르주의 블라고베셴스크에서는 3월에 아타만 이반 가모프의 반란이 진압되었는데, 영어 문헌이 인용하는 테플랴코프의 연구에 따르면 적위대가 도시를 차지한 뒤 주민 천여 명이 죽었다. 첸트로시비리와 하바롭스크의 인민위원회의는 끝내 손발을 맞추지 못했고, 첸트로시비리는 극동 쪽의 「분리주의」를 비판했다. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Krasnoshchyokov) [4](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BD%D0%BE%D1%89%D1%91%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2,_%D0%90%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%81%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4%D1%80_%D0%9C%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87) [5](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%B8%D0%BC-%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87,_%D0%90%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%81%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4%D1%80%D0%B0_%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BD%D0%B0) [1](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B1%D0%B8%D1%80%D1%8C) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_intervention_in_Siberia) [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolayevsk_incident)

시베리아에서 소비에트에 맞선 정치 세력은 백군 장교만이 아니었다. 시베리아 자치를 주장하는 지역주의자와 사회혁명당이 1918년 1월 말 톰스크에 시베리아 지역 두마를 소집하려 하자, 톰스크를 장악한 첸트로시비리 쪽 볼셰비키는 1월 25~26일 밤 대의원들을 체포하고 두마 해산을 결정했다. 체포를 피한 대의원들은 사회혁명당원 표트르 데르베르를 수반으로 하는 시베리아 임시정부를 세웠다. 이 정부는 3월 하얼빈으로 옮겨 갔다가 6월에야 블라디보스토크에 자리를 잡았고, 떠나기 전 서시베리아에 사회혁명당원 네 명으로 이루어진 지하 서시베리아 위원부를 남겨 두었다. 1918년 4월 5일 첸트로시비리는 외국의 개입에 항의하며 시베리아에 계엄을 선포하고 혁명 참모부를 세웠으며, 옴스크·이르쿠츠크·프리아무르 군관구를 하나로 묶은 군사 위원부와 시베리아 체카를 만들었다. 그러나 소비에트들이 가진 무장력은 적위대와 국제주의자 부대, 그리고 막 편성되기 시작한 붉은 군대 부대가 전부였다. 그들이 마주한 것은 철도를 따라 길게 늘어선, 4만~5만 명으로 추산되는 무장 부대였다. ## 군단의 반란과 시베리아의 정부들 (1918년 5~11월) {russia czechoslovakia}

1918년 5월 첼랴빈스크에서 시작된 체코슬로바키아 군단과 볼셰비키의 충돌은 상위 사건에서 다루었다. 시베리아에서 그 결과는 빨랐다. 5월 25일 트로츠키의 무장 해제 명령이 떨어진 무렵 노보니콜라옙스크에서는 라돌라 가이다가 봉기를 조직했고, 군단은 마리인스크, 니즈네우딘스크, 칸스크 같은 철도 도시를 차례로 차지했다. 이르쿠츠크에서도 5월 26일 첸트로시비리가 인노켄티옙스카야역에 도착하는 군단 열차를 무장 해제하기로 결정하자 역에서 전투가 벌어져 50명이 죽었다. 이튿날 첸트로시비리 대표단이 강화를 맺었지만 싸움은 6월에 다시 번졌다. 6월 6일 옴스크가 백군에게 넘어갔고, 6월 말에는 미하일 디테릭스가 이끄는 군단 부대가 블라디보스토크의 볼셰비키 행정부를 무너뜨렸다. 군단은 7월 6일 블라디보스토크를 연합국 보호령으로 선포하고, 서쪽에서 싸우는 동료들을 도우러 철도를 되짚어 갔다. 영어 문헌에 따르면 8월 무렵 우랄의 전선에서는 붉은 군대 약 6만 5천 명이 군단과 반볼셰비키 러시아군 약 5만 명과 맞서고 있었다. [10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolt_of_the_Czechoslovak_Legion) [11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czechoslovak_Legion) [12](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%93%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%B4%D0%B0,_%D0%A0%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B0) [1](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B1%D0%B8%D1%80%D1%8C) [9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Siberian_Government_(Omsk))

군단이 철도를 쥐자 시베리아의 소비에트 권력은 버티지 못했다. 6월 13일에는 니즈네우딘스크에서 칸스크까지의 선로가 이미 군단 손에 있었고, 첸트로시비리는 7월 11일 이르쿠츠크를 버리고 베르흐네우딘스크로 물러났다. 가이다는 이르쿠츠크에 이어 치타까지 진격했다. 군단이 바이칼호 남단의 터널 지대에서 볼셰비키 부대를 깨뜨린 것이 8월 말이었고, 그 뒤 군단은 블라디보스토크 쪽으로 계속 나아갔다. 첸트로시비리는 8월 16일 치타로, 다시 바깥으로 쫓겨났다. 8월 28일 우룰가역에서 열린 당·소비에트·군 간부 회의는 시베리아 인민위원회의를 해산하고, 조직된 전선의 싸움을 그만두는 대신 합법·비합법의 모든 방법으로 싸우기로 결정했다. 국제주의자 부대는 무기와 물자를 받아 숲으로 들어갔다. 극동에서도 하바롭스크가 9월 5일 아타만 칼미코프에게 넘어가면서 크라스노쇼코프의 인민위원회의가 무너졌다. 그는 타이가를 건너 붉은 군대 지역으로 가려다 사마라 부근에서 붙잡혀 이르쿠츠크 감옥으로 보내졌고, 1919년 12월에야 풀려났다. 라조는 지하로 들어가 블라디보스토크의 지하 당 위원회에서 일했다. 소비에트가 물러난 자리를 두고는 반볼셰비키 정부들이 다투었다. 옴스크에서는 6월 내내 협상이 이어진 끝에 6월 30일 표트르 볼로고츠키를 의장으로 하는 새 각료회의, 곧 옴스크의 시베리아 임시정부가 출범했다. 한 러시아 장군은 이를 「평화롭게 이루어진 쿠데타」라고 불렀다. 사회혁명당 색채가 짙은 데르베르 정부를 군대가 원하지 않았기 때문이다. 블라디보스토크의 데르베르 정부는 6월 29일 「시베리아 자치 임시정부」로 이름을 바꾸고 자신이 시베리아의 중앙 권력이라고 선언했지만, 군사력과 지지는 옴스크에 있었다. 옴스크 정부는 7월 4일 「시베리아의 국가적 독립에 관한」 선언을 채택했고, 볼가의 코무치와는 관세 전쟁과 경계 분쟁을 벌였다. 군단의 압력도 작용한 가운데 9월 8~23일 우파에서 국가 회의가 열려 5인 디렉토리아, 곧 전러시아 임시정부가 세워졌다. 디렉토리아는 10월 옴스크로 옮겼지만 행정은 각료 14명 중 10명이 옛 시베리아 정부 출신인 각료회의에 기댔다. 11월 18일 옴스크 쿠데타로 니콜라이 압크센티예프와 블라디미르 젠지노프가 체포되고 알렉산드르 콜차크가 최고 통치자가 된 과정은 상위 사건에서 다루었다. ## 콜차크의 후방: 아타만과 철도 {russia}

옴스크 정권의 권위는 바이칼호 동쪽에서 거의 통하지 않았다. 자바이칼 카자크 출신 그리고리 세묘노프는 1918년 1월 만저우리를 거점으로 자바이칼을 침공했다가 밀려났지만, 영국 외무부가 조건 없이 매달 1만 파운드를 주기로 하고 프랑스도 자금을 댔으며 일본은 그의 사령부에 정보 장교를 두었다. 영국 보조금이 끊길 무렵 그는 사실상 일본의 꼭두각시가 되어 있었다. 8월 자바이칼을 장악한 세묘노프 부대는 9월 6일 치타를 점령하면서 주민 348명을 학살했고, 치타가 그의 수도가 되었다. 그의 영역은 바이칼호 부근 베르흐네우딘스크에서 실카강과 스레텐스크, 만저우리까지 뻗었다. 콜차크가 최고 통치자가 되자 세묘노프는 복종을 거부했다. 콜차크는 군대를 보내 그를 제거하려 했지만 일본군의 보호 때문에 단념했고, 1919년 10월에는 오히려 그를 자바이칼 지역 총사령관으로 인정했다. 세묘노프는 화물이 무엇이든, 누구를 위한 것이든 열차를 세워 돈을 뜯어낸 「노상강도」로 묘사되었다. 그의 부하이던 로만 폰 운게른슈테른베르크가 다우리야역에 만든 요새는 처형된 이들의 뼈가 쌓인 「고문 센터」로 알려졌다. [17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigory_Semyonov_(general)) [18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_von_Ungern-Sternberg)

우수리 카자크의 아타만 이반 칼미코프는 1918년 9월 5일 하바롭스크를 점령하고 하바롭스크 수비대장이 되었다. 러시아어 문헌에 따르면 그해 9월 하바롭스크에서는 재판 없는 대량 총살이 여러 차례 있었고, 11월에도 약 20명이 같은 식으로 죽었다. 9월 4일 백군과 일본군에게 체포된 알렉산드라 킴도 칼미코프의 카자크들에게 총살되었다. 칼미코프 부대의 약탈과 살인, 강간은 백군 안에서도 분노를 샀고 콜차크 자신도 그중 하나였다. 그의 부대는 국제 적십자 대표인 스웨덴인과 노르웨이인을 살해하고 아무르강의 중국 포함을 포격했다는 혐의를 받았다. 1920년 2월 고립된 칼미코프는 하바롭스크 국립은행 지점의 금 622킬로그램을 일본군 사령부에 몰래 넘긴 뒤 중국 땅으로 달아났고, 중국 당국에 붙잡혀 있다가 9월 탈주하던 중 사살되었다. 피해 규모는 출처마다 다르다. 영어 문헌은 미 육군 정보부가 세묘노프에게 한 해 동안 3만 명을 처형한 책임이 있다고 추산했다고 쓰고, 러시아어 문헌은 윌리엄 그레이브스의 보고서가 4만 명이라고 했다고 쓴다. 트로이츠코사프스크 감옥에서는 1919년 12월 24일부터 1920년 1월 10일 사이에 약 1,500명이 살해되었다. 그레이브스는 훗날 이렇게 증언했다. 「세묘노프와 칼미코프의 병사들은 일본군의 보호 아래 들짐승처럼 나라를 돌아다니며 사람들을 죽이고 약탈했고, 일본이 원했다면 이 살인은 어느 날이든 멈출 수 있었다. … 동시베리아에서 반볼셰비키가 한 사람을 죽일 때마다 볼셰비키는 백 명을 죽였다고 세상은 믿지만, 실은 그 반대였다고 말해도 안전하다.」 콜차크가 1920년 1월 4일 극동의 군권을 세묘노프에게 넘겼을 때에도 실권은 블라디보스토크의 세르게이 로자노프, 하바롭스크의 칼미코프, 블라고베셴스크의 아무르 아타만에게 나뉘어 있었고, 이들 모두 일본의 돈과 병력에 기댔다. 이 지역을 하나로 묶은 것은 시베리아 횡단 철도였다. 1919년 미국 철도 기술자 존 프랭크 스티븐스가 동청 철도와 시베리아 철도의 관리·운영을 맡은 연합국 기술위원회를 이끌었는데, 동청 철도가 일본 손에 넘어가는 것을 막는 것도 그 역할이었다. 연합국 철도 협정에 따라 미군은 블라디보스토크에서 우수리스크까지와 베르흐네우딘스크 부근 구간을 지켰고, 1919년 1월 27일 군단 사령관 얀 시로비는 노보니콜라옙스크와 이르쿠츠크 사이의 선로를 체코슬로바키아 작전 구역으로 선언했다. ## 연합국 개입: 일본과 미국, 그리고 영국 {japan usa uk}

극동 개입의 첫 신호는 경쟁이었다. 영국이 일본과 상의 없이 미국에 블라디보스토크 공동 개입을 타진하고 홍콩의 순양함 서퍽을 보내자, 데라우치 마사타케 총리는 해군에 먼저 도착하라고 명령했다. 전함 이와미는 1918년 1월 12일 서퍽보다 이틀 앞서 블라디보스토크에 닿았다. 무장한 무리가 일본인 상점을 약탈하고 주인을 죽이자 일본은 해병을 상륙시켰다. 일본 육군 참모본부는 1918년 2월 「시베리아 계획 위원회」를 만들어 제정 붕괴를 시베리아를 떼어 내 완충국을 세울 기회로 보았다. 7월 우드로 윌슨은 체코슬로바키아 군단 구출을 명분으로 일본에 2만 5천 명 규모 국제 연합군의 일부로 7천 명을 보내 달라고 요청했다. 데라우치 내각은 의회의 격론 끝에 1만 2천 명을 보내되 일본의 단독 지휘를 받게 하기로 했다. 그러나 실제 파병은 그 몇 배였다. 8월 말까지 1만 8천 명이 블라디보스토크에 상륙하고 6천 명이 만주를 거쳐 만저우리로 갔으며, 11월 초까지 7만 명이 넘었다. 8월 18일 오타니 기쿠조 장군이 연합군 전체의 지휘를 맡았다. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_intervention_in_Siberia) [13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_intervention)

다른 나라들의 병력은 훨씬 작았다. 1918년 8월 3일 노동조합 지도자이자 자유당 의원인 존 워드 중령의 영국 미들섹스 연대 대대가 연합군 지상군으로는 처음 블라디보스토크에 상륙했고, 영국은 모두 1,800명을 두 대대로 보내고 앨프리드 녹스 장군의 군사 사절단 500명을 따로 두었다. 프랑스는 인도차이나의 식민지 연대 500명을, 캐나다는 4,192명을 보냈다. 캐나다군 수송선은 프랑스계 병사 중심의 두 중대가 빅토리아에서 반란을 일으켜 출항이 늦어졌고, 대부분 블라디보스토크에 머물다 1919년 6월 5일까지 모두 돌아갔다. 중국·이탈리아·폴란드·세르비아·루마니아 부대도 왔다. 우수리 전선에서는 8월 23~25일 두홉스카야 전투에서 일본군 지휘를 받는 연합군이 영국 장갑열차의 지원 속에 볼셰비키 장갑열차 다섯 대를 공격해 그곳의 조직적 저항을 끝냈다. 일본군 전사자는 600명이었다. 영국·프랑스·이탈리아 부대가 군단과 함께 우랄 쪽으로 간 반면, 일본군은 바이칼호 서쪽으로 가기를 거부했다. 11월까지 일본군은 연해주의 모든 항구와 치타 동쪽 시베리아의 주요 도시를 차지했다. [13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_intervention) [23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Siberian_Expeditionary_Force)

미국 시베리아 원정군은 윌리엄 그레이브스 소장이 지휘했고 병력은 출처에 따라 7,950명에서 8,763명이었다. 첫 3천 명은 8월 15~21일 블라디보스토크에 내렸고 그레이브스는 9월 초에 도착했다. 그는 자신의 임무가 미국이 보낸 물자를 지키고 군단의 철수를 돕는 것일 뿐 볼셰비키와 싸우는 것이 아니라고 보았다. 그는 「내정 불간섭」과 「완전 중립」을 내세워 콜차크 쪽과 붉은 파르티잔을 똑같이 대했고, 미군 구역에서는 수찬 탄광 노동자들의 집회를 막지 않았다. 영국의 워드는 미국이 중립 지대에서 볼셰비키를 「보호」해 그들이 습격 기지를 두게 했다고 비난했고, 세묘노프는 그레이브스가 붉은 쪽을 돕는다고 했다. 그레이브스는 일본이 바이칼 동쪽 아무르 지역을 병합하려 한다고 의심했고, 미군이 바이칼 동쪽에 남은 것도 일본을 감시하기 위해서였다. 미일 마찰은 실제 충돌 직전까지 갔다. 철도역 예브게니옙카에서는 미군 보초가 일본 병사를 찔러 양측이 총을 겨눴고, 1919년 10월 이만에서는 로자노프 부대가 붙잡은 미군 상병이 칼미코프 사령부에서 채찍질을 당했다. 일본이 시베리아에서 노린 것은 백군의 서진보다 가까운 러시아·중국 영토의 상업적 지배였다는 평가도 있다. ## 파르티잔 전쟁과 옴스크 정권의 붕괴 {russia}

콜차크 정권의 징발과 동원, 처벌은 시베리아 농촌을 봉기로 몰았다. 1918년 12월 3일 정부는 「최고 통치자의 체제와 통치를 지키기 위해」 형법을 고쳐 사형과 군법회의 처벌을 넓혔다. 예니세이 지역에서 세르게이 로자노프 장군은 「주민이 무기를 들고 군대를 맞는 마을은 불태우고 성인 남자는 예외 없이 총살하라」고 명령했다. 영어 문헌에 인용된 멘셰비키 기관지는 야전 군법회의와 토벌대에 농민 4천 명이 희생되었다고 주장했다. 저항은 1918년 12월에 시작되었다. 12월 2일 크라스노야르스크군 스테프노바제이 읍에서 지하 조직이 읍사무소를 장악하고 혁명위원회를 세웠고, 같은 달 칸스크군 타세예보에서는 바실리 야코벤코가 봉기를 이끌었다. 타세예보 파르티잔 공화국은 1919년 1월부터 군사혁명 참모부를 두었고 병력이 최대 1만 5천 명에 이르렀다. 아친스크에서는 4개의 성 게오르기 십자 훈장을 받은 전 이등대위 표트르 셰틴킨이 1919년 1월 5일 무장 행동을 시작했다. 그는 4월 알렉산드르 크랍첸코의 부대와 합쳐 파르티잔군 참모장이 되었고, 이 군대는 타이가를 700킬로미터 남하해 9월 13일 미누신스크를 차지했다. 11월에는 병력이 1만 8천 명에 이르렀다. 알타이의 초원에서는 성 게오르기 십자 훈장을 받은 농민 출신 전신병 예핌 마몬토프가 파르티잔을 이끌었다. 그는 1918년 9월 시베리아 임시정부에 맞선 초르니돌 농민 봉기를 도우러 나섰다가 숨어 지냈고, 1919년 봄부터 슬라브고로드군 남부에서 기병 부대를 이끌었다. 콜차크가 알타이 전체를 포함한 서시베리아 18개 군을 작전 지역으로 선포하고 토벌대를 보내자, 1919년 10월 7일 우티치예 마을에 모인 지휘관들은 부대를 합쳐 서시베리아 농민 붉은 군대를 만들고 마몬토프를 총사령관으로 뽑았다. 이 군대의 규모는 영어 문헌이 2만 5천 명, 러시아어 문헌이 1919년 말 25개 연대 약 5만 명이라고 쓴다. 파르티잔은 12월 6~7일 바르나울 공격에 실패했지만 거의 포위된 백군은 12월 10일 밤 도시를 버렸다. 영어 문헌에 따르면 1919년 가을 시베리아 파르티잔 약 10만 명이 붉은 군대가 오기도 전에 넓은 지역을 장악했고, 1920년 2월에는 약 2만 명이 아무르주를 차지했다. 정규군이 들어온 뒤 파르티잔 부대는 해산되거나 붉은 군대에 편입되었다. 크랍첸코와 셰틴킨의 부대는 1920년 1월 제5군의 예니세이 소총 사단이 되었다. 1919년 가을 전선이 무너지자 후방도 갈라졌다. 군단은 콜차크 쪽 군의 행태를 고발하는 각서를 11월 15일 연합국 대표들에게 냈고, 이틀 뒤 가이다가 블라디보스토크에서 콜차크에 맞서 봉기했다가 실패했다. 그레이브스는 이 음모에서 사회혁명당 지하 조직과 군단 사이의 연락을 맡았다고 러시아어 문헌은 쓴다. 이르쿠츠크에서는 11월 12일 시베리아 젬스트보와 시 두마 회의가 사회혁명당·멘셰비키·젬스트보·농민 단체로 이루어진 정치센터를 뽑았다. 정치센터는 콜차크 정권 타도와 공산주의자의 승리 저지, 동시베리아와 극동의 민주적 완충국 수립을 내걸었고, 봉기를 일으켜 1920년 1월 5일까지 이르쿠츠크를 장악했다. 블라디미르 카펠의 군대가 시베리아 대빙원 행군으로 다가오는 가운데, 군단은 동쪽으로 가는 길을 얻는 대가로 콜차크를 정치센터에 넘겼다. 정치센터는 1월 23일 볼셰비키 군사혁명위원회에 권력을 넘겼고, 콜차크는 2월 7일 총살되었다. 같은 날 군단은 쿠틴에서 제5군과 휴전해 블라디보스토크까지의 통행을 보장받는 대신 남은 금괴를 이르쿠츠크 당국에 남겼다. 마지막 단계도 시베리아의 겨울만큼 잔혹했다. 1919년 12월 세묘노프가 이르쿠츠크로 보낸 부대는 인질 31명을 잡아 바이칼호의 쇄빙선으로 끌고 가, 1월 5일 나무망치로 한 사람씩 때려 죽이고 물에 던졌다. 카펠의 군대와 그 가족 약 3만 명은 크라스노야르스크 봉기를 피해 얼어붙은 바이칼호를 건너 치타로 향했고, 카펠은 동상과 폐렴으로 1월 26일 죽었다. 쫓아온 제5군은 겐리흐 에이헤가 지휘했다. 그러나 러시아 공산당 중앙위원회는 일본과의 충돌을 피하려고 이르쿠츠크 너머로 진격하지 말라고 명령했다. 마지막 군단 열차는 3월 1일 이르쿠츠크를 지났고, 군단원들은 1920년 9월까지 블라디보스토크에서 36차례 배로 떠났다. 함께 떠난 사람은 병사 5만 6,455명과 장교 3,004명을 포함해 6만 7,739명이었고, 러시아에서 전사한 군단원은 4,112명이었다. 콜차크 정부 각료들을 재판한 1920년 5월의 시베리아 특별 혁명재판소에는 셰틴킨과 마몬토프가 재판관으로 참여했다. ## 극동공화국과 일본: 1920년 {russia japan}

이르쿠츠크 감옥에서 풀려난 크라스노쇼코프는 1920년 1월 전선을 넘어 톰스크의 붉은 군대 사령부로 가서 레닌을 설득했다. 연합군이 체면을 잃지 않고 철수할 수 있도록 극동에 완충국을 세우자는 것이었다. 비슷한 제안은 정치센터에서도 나왔고, 러시아어 문헌은 이반 스미르노프와 크라스노쇼코프를 구상자로 든다. 레닌과 모스크바 지도부는 당원 약 4천 명이 직접 권력을 잡을 수 있다는 현지 공산당원들의 반대를 물리쳤다. 일본군 약 7만 명과 미군이 있는 곳에서 소비에트 권력 선포는 도발이 될 수 있었고, 서쪽에서는 폴란드와의 전쟁이 다가오고 있었다. 2월 18일 정치국은 완충국을 승인했고, 모스크바는 극동공화국을 「동쪽의 브레스트-리토프스크 조약」, 곧 숨 돌릴 틈으로 보았다. 4월 6일 베르흐네우딘스크의 제헌 대회가 극동공화국을 선포했다. 크라스노쇼코프는 헌법을 먼저 영어로 쓴 뒤 러시아어로 옮겼고 정부 수반 겸 외무장관이 되었다. 그러나 다당제 민주공화국이라는 겉모습과 달리 공화국은 처음부터 모스크바의 재정·외교·군사 지원에 기댔고, 공산당의 극동국이 이를 이끌었다. 연해주에서는 다른 길이 시도되었다. 1920년 1월 31일 블라디보스토크 봉기로 콜차크의 대리인 로자노프가 쫓겨나고 연해주 젬스트보 정부가 들어섰는데, 이 연립 정부에서는 볼셰비키 세르게이 라조와 표트르 니키포로프가 주도권을 쥐었다. 라조는 루스키섬의 사관학교 생도들 앞에 홀로 무기 없이 나서 연설해 그들을 봉기 편으로 돌렸다. 일본군은 2월 4일 중립을 선언했지만, 블라디보스토크 정부가 볼셰비키 손에 들어가고 소비에트 권력을 선포하려 하자 4월 4~5일 연해주 전역에서 혁명 세력을 기습했다. 라조는 4~5일 밤 일본군에게 체포되었고, 5월 말 동료 루츠키, 시비르체프와 함께 백군 카자크에게 넘겨져 죽었다. 기관차 화실에서 산 채로 불태워졌다는 이야기가 널리 퍼졌지만, 최근 러시아 극동사 연구는 이를 전설로 보고 그가 다른 이름으로 에게르셸드에서 총살된 뒤 불태워졌다는 기록을 든다. 일본군의 공격으로 흩어진 파르티잔은 한동안 반격하지 못했고, 블라디보스토크를 중심으로 완충국을 세우려던 계획은 무너졌다. 미군 마지막 부대는 이미 4월 1일 떠났고, 일본은 이제 홀로 남은 점령국이었다. 아무르강 하구의 금광 도시 니콜라옙스크나아무레에서는 이 시기 최악의 비극이 벌어졌다. 1920년 1월 아나키스트 야코프 트랴피친이 이끄는 수천 명의 파르티잔이 도시를 포위했다. 도시에는 일본 수비대 350명, 일본 민간인 약 450명, 백군 약 300명이 있었다. 2월 28일 휴전으로 파르티잔이 입성한 뒤 주민 체포와 처형이 시작되었고, 3월 12일 일본군이 기습하자 나흘간의 전투 끝에 일본 수비대가 전멸하고 영사관도 불탔다. 파르티잔도 최대 500명이 죽었다. 5월 하순 일본 원군이 다가오자 트랴피친의 본부는 남은 일본인 포로 129명과 수감자들을 처형하고 주민을 타이가로 끌고 간 뒤 도시를 불태웠다. 러시아어 문헌에 따르면 주거용 건물 1,165채 가운데 35채만 남았다. 희생자 수는 엇갈린다. 일본 대표는 워싱턴 회의에서 일본인 700명 이상이 죽었다고 했고, 영어 문헌이 인용하는 사할린 당국의 추산은 굶주림을 포함해 지역 전체에서 1만~1만 5천 명이 사라졌다는 것이다. 트랴피친은 7월 케르비에서 파르티잔 법정에 서서 총살되었다. 일본은 이 사건을 이유로 북사할린을 점령했는데, 러시아어 문헌은 점령이 5월의 처형보다 앞선 4월 22일에 시작되었다고 지적한다. [39](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9D%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82) [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolayevsk_incident) [37](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_Eastern_Republic)

그래도 완충국 구상은 목적을 이루었다. 일본군 사령부는 5월 11일 극동공화국을 인정했고, 소비에트 러시아도 곧 승인했다. 공고타역에서 5월 24일부터 열린 협상 끝에 7월 15일 일본 원정군과 극동공화국은 베르흐네우딘스크와 치타 사이에 중립 지대를 두는 공고타 협정을 맺었다. 파르티잔의 끊임없는 압박을 받던 일본군은 이로써 체면을 잃지 않고 자바이칼에서 물러날 수 있었고, 10월 15일 철수를 마쳤다. 후원자를 잃은 세묘노프의 「러시아 동부 변경」은 에이헤의 제5군과 극동공화국 인민혁명군, 파르티잔의 공세에 무너졌다. 10월 22일 인민혁명군과 파르티잔이 치타에 들어갔고 세묘노프는 비행기로 만주에 달아났다. 같은 무렵 일본군이 하바롭스크에서도 철수했다. 10월 28일부터 11월 11일까지 치타에서 열린 회의에서 서·동 자바이칼, 아무르, 연해주, 사할린의 다섯 지역 정부 대표들이 통합을 확정하고 수도를 치타로 옮겼다. 1921년 1월 9일 선거로 뽑힌 제헌의회는 4월 27일 미국 헌법과 닮은 헌법을 채택했다. 다수는 공산당 92석과 그 편에 선 농민 다수파 183석이었다.
